newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores strike call sees mixed response.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores strike call sees mixed response.

text.p: Early reports from Brazil's key soybeans and coffee ports showed a mixed response to a call for a national stevedores strike due to have begun at 0700 local/1000GMT today.
In Paranagua, Brazil's main soybean port, a union official said stevedores were still working and that he knew of no plans to strike.

In Vitoria, Brazil's second largest coffee port after Santos, a union offical said the union had only notified the port authority yesterday of the strike and so would only hold a 24-hour stoppage as of 0700 local Saturday.
In Rio de Janeiro, the country's third main coffee exit point, the strike had begun and loading and unloading was virtually paralysed, a port authority official said.
The national strike was called to show support for colleagues in Santos who began an indefinite strike at 0700 local April 15.
The Santos workers are protesting against local steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers in its private terminal at the port.
Fresh talks between Cosipa and union representatives are scheduled to be held at 0900 local Friday, Cosipa said on Thursday.
Stevedore federation officials were not immediately available to comment on the national strike.
